subject: Post-demo: Brightside vector assessment + migration next steps

Subject: Post-demo: Brightside vector assessment + migration next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the context on Brightside's recommendation search flows. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Summary of what we heard:
- Search/ranking use case: hybrid semantic + lexical pipeline, initial index rebuild nightly with real-time upserts for recent items.
- Current provider: VectorCloud (proprietary) storing vectors at 2048 dims; embeddings stored as float32 JSONL; ingestion is batch-first.
- Scale: ~18M active items, daily add rate ~12k, peak QPS for search ~300 (bursty, retail hours).
- Wants: reduce index size, improve recall for long-tail queries, and enable a reranker stage for top-10 results.

Redwood recommendations (initial):
1) Vector dimension: we recommend migrating to 1536 dims (good tradeoff for quality vs storage). If you need smaller payloads for mobile, evaluate 1024 for a small fidelity drop.
2) Normalization: L2-normalize at index time (most plug-and-play with our dot-product fast-path).
3) Batching: aim for ingestion batches of 64–256 items depending on latency SLOs; 128 is a good starting point for nightly rebuilds, 64 for nearline upserts.
4) Migration strategy: stream-conversion approach — bulk convert historical vectors offline to Redwood format + keep hybrid indexing during cutover. We'll provide a migration helper script for VectorCloud exports.
5) Reranker: run a lightweight transformer re-ranker (sequence-to-score) on top-10 candidates; recommend measuring latency budget before committing to heavy rerankers at search-time.
6) Auth & routing: API key for dev/POC, mTLS or scoped service accounts for production; route traffic to us-west for lower latency and fall back to us-east in peak.
7) SDK & structured output: Redwood SDK supports structured tool-calling and typed outputs if you plan to surface product attributes from LLM outputs (we can show examples for your QA JSON schema).

Attachments referenced: MAP-Brightside-v1.pdf (mutual action plan), embeddings_sample.csv (3 sample records), brightside_current_vectors.jsonl (your export you shared).

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Tech deep-dive (60m) with your eng-ops + our SEs next week — Ben/Rishi to join.
- We’ll share: (a) a migration helper script, (b) a Redwood SDK snippet for auth + batching, (c) cost estimate for a 30-day proof-of-concept.
- You share: an example index export and any constraints on latency or retention (you attached the export which is great).

Proposed windows: Tue/Wed next week afternoon PT. Let me know which works and we’ll send a calendar invite.

—

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifying questions from engineering: 

1) Tokenization mismatch: our current pipeline embeds whole descriptions (~220 tokens). If we switch dims from 2048 -> 1536, do we need to change how we chunk or just retrain embeddings?
2) Migration safety: can Redwood serve hybrid traffic (VectorCloud + Redwood) while we backfill? We can’t afford search downtime during conversion.
3) Reranker latency: our SLA for front-page search is 120ms p95; is the re-ranker feasible for top-10 with that constraint?
4) Do you have an existing conversion script for VectorCloud JSONL -> Redwood binary/quantized format? We attached our current_vectors.jsonl (first ~500) to this thread.

Appreciate if Ben and Rishi can weigh in with technical tradeoffs.

—
Michael Tan

m.tan@brightside.ai

Michael — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers + proposed approach: 

1) Tokenization & embedding dims: you can keep your current tokenization and just re-embed to 1536. Most transformer-based encoders have a smooth degradation between dims; we recommend running a 1% quality sample comparison (we can do this for you with a seed set). Retraining is not strictly required if you move to a Redwood-hosted variant (we provide model variants pre-trained at the target dims or we can quantize).

2) Hybrid serving during backfill: yes — Redwood supports dual-routing. During migration we create a read-through layer that queries Redwood first (for migrated items) and falls back to VectorCloud for items still pending. This keeps search continuity while you backfill.

3) Reranker latency: top-10 rerank with a small cross-encoder can fit under 120ms p95 if you colocate the reranker with the search path and constrain the model (distilled cross-encoder or a light MLP reranker). We'll run a latency profile during POC; if it exceeds budget we recommend async re-rank with cached scores for less urgent flows.

4) Conversion helper: attached is a starter script (redwood_sdk_snippet.txt) — it includes a streaming converter that reads VectorCloud JSONL and writes quantized int8 payloads compatible with our import tool. For your first pass, run it offline on a subset, validate recall against your seed queries, then bulk-run for the rest.

Notes on batching & memory sizing: when ingesting quantized vectors, 128 item batches are efficient for GPU pipelines; if you need very low-latency single-item upserts we suggest smaller nearline batches of 16–32 and a single-item write path.

Auth & routing: POC will use scoped API keys (can be restricted to index IDs). For production we recommend mTLS + short-lived service tokens via your KMS. Routing policy: route by region then cost to preserve performance during peak, Redwood Console will surface per-route latency heatmaps.

SDK snippet & link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/quickstart#embeddings (see attached snippet).
